decisions.choice: for you have said: the reason for what follows in verses 21-23
alternatives: Since you have said ... (answered in verse 16)
decisions.reason: The sentence begins "because" or "since", and the answer to it comes in verses 21-23, which name two of these prophets in Babylon and their fate. Verses 16-20 stand between, as a message about those still in Jerusalem. Some read verse 15 with verse 16 instead: since you trust these prophets, hear what the LORD says about Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: prophets in Babylon: men among the exiles who spoke in the LORD's name
decisions.reason: There were prophets among the exiles who promised a quick return (verses 8-9, 21, 24-28). Ezekiel also prophesied among the exiles from 593 BC (Ezekiel 1:1-3), but the letter speaks of the prophets the exiles trusted against Jeremiah's word.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks
decisions.reason: The exiles' words are quoted inside the letter, so they take single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: here in Babylon (Balanced, Readable); has given us (Readable)
decisions.reason: The speakers are in Babylon, so Balanced and Readable say "here". Readable says "given" for "raised up".

source.text: כִּי־כֹ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הַיּוֹשֵׁב֙ אֶל־כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֔ד וְאֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֔ם הַיּוֹשֵׁ֖ב בָּעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את אֲחֵיכֶ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־יָצְא֥וּ אִתְּכֶ֖ם בַּגּוֹלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus says Yahweh concerning the king who sits on [the] throne of David and concerning all the people who dwell in the city the this, your brothers who not went out with you into the exile:

en.L: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning the king who sits on the throne of David and concerning all the people who live in this city, your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} who did not go out with you into exile:
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this about the king who sits on David's throne and about all the people who live in this city, your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} who did not go with you into exile:
en.R: But this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says about the king who rules from David's throne, and about all the people who still live in Jerusalem, your relatives who were not taken away with you:

es.L: Porque así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} acerca del rey que se sienta en el trono de David, y acerca de todo el pueblo que habita en esta ciudad, {{plural_you:sus hermanos|vuestros hermanos}} que no salieron con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} al destierro:
es.B: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto acerca del rey que se sienta en el trono de David, y acerca de todo el pueblo que vive en esta ciudad, {{plural_you:sus hermanos|vuestros hermanos}} que no fueron con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} al destierro:
es.R: Pero esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} acerca del rey que gobierna desde el trono de David, y acerca de toda la gente que todavía vive en Jerusalén, {{plural_you:sus parientes|vuestros parientes}} que no fueron llevados con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}:

fr.L: Car ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au sujet du roi qui siège sur le trône de David et au sujet de tout le peuple qui habite cette ville, vos {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} qui ne sont pas partis avec vous en exil :
fr.B: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci au sujet du roi qui siège sur le trône de David et au sujet de tout le peuple qui habite cette ville, vos {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} qui ne sont pas partis avec vous en exil :
fr.R: Mais voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au sujet du roi qui règne sur le trône de David et de tous les gens qui habitent encore à Jérusalem, vos proches qu’on n’a pas emmenés avec vous :

sw.L: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi kuhusu mfalme aketiye juu ya kiti cha enzi cha Daudi, na kuhusu watu wote wakaao katika mji huu, ndugu zenu ambao hawakutoka pamoja nanyi kwenda uhamishoni:
sw.B: Lakini hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo kuhusu mfalme aketiye juu ya kiti cha enzi cha Daudi, na kuhusu watu wote wanaoishi katika mji huu, ndugu zenu ambao hawakwenda pamoja nanyi uhamishoni:
sw.R: Lakini hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema kuhusu mfalme anayetawala kutoka kiti cha enzi cha Daudi, na kuhusu watu wote ambao bado wanaishi Yerusalemu, ndugu zenu ambao hawakuchukuliwa pamoja nanyi:

decisions.choice: verses 16-20 are not in the Greek translation
decisions.reason: The Greek translation goes straight from verse 15 to verse 21. Verses 16-20 repeat words found elsewhere in Jeremiah (24:8-10; 25:4), and some think they were added to the letter; others think the Greek lost them because verse 15 and verse 20 both end with "Babylon". The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: the king who sits on the throne of David: Zedekiah
decisions.reason: The king still reigning in Jerusalem was Zedekiah (verse 3), who had been put on the throne by Babylon in place of Jeconiah.

decisions.choice: for: the message about Jerusalem answers the exiles' hopes
decisions.reason: The exiles' prophets said that they would soon return (verses 8-9, 15). God's word about those left in Jerusalem shows why that cannot be: the city itself and its king are under judgment, so there will be no quick return to it.

decisions.choice: your brothers: your fellow countrymen, your own people
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means fellow members of the people of Judah, men and women, those who were not taken to Babylon in 597 BC.

decisions.choice: your brothers and sisters (gender setting)
decisions.reason: The word means all their kin who stayed behind, women as well as men, so Literal and Balanced give an inclusive default with "brothers" as the alternative. Readable says "relatives".

decisions.choice: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names the city meant by "this city", since the exiles hearing the letter were in Babylon.

decisions.choice: sus hermanos
decisions.reason: Spanish "hermanos" already includes women, so no gender span is used where the English has one, as the terms note sets.

decisions.choice: ndugu zenu
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so Swahili needs no gender alternative here.

source.text: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִנְנִי֙ מְשַׁלֵּ֣חַ בָּ֔ם אֶת־הַחֶ֖רֶב אֶת־הָרָעָ֣ב וְאֶת־הַדָּ֑בֶר וְנָתַתִּ֣י אוֹתָ֗ם כַּתְּאֵנִים֙ הַשֹּׁ֣עָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־תֵאָכַ֖לְנָה מֵרֹֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts: Behold, I [am] sending on them the sword, the famine and the pestilence, and I will make them like the figs the horrid which not can be eaten from badness.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Look, I am sending against them the sword, the famine and the pestilence, and I will make them like horrid figs that cannot be eaten because of [their] badness.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: I am about to send the sword, famine and plague against them, and I will make them like rotten figs, so bad that they cannot be eaten.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: I am going to send war, famine and disease against them. I will make them like rotten figs that are too bad to eat.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: He aquí, yo envío contra ellos la espada, el hambre y la peste, y los pondré como los higos podridos que no se pueden comer de tan malos.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: Voy a enviar contra ellos la espada, el hambre y la peste, y los haré como higos podridos, tan malos que no se pueden comer.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: Voy a enviar contra ellos la guerra, el hambre y las enfermedades. Los haré como higos podridos que no se pueden comer de tan malos.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Voici, j’envoie contre eux l’épée, la famine et la peste, et je les rendrai pareils à des figues infectes qu’on ne peut pas manger tant elles sont mauvaises.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : Je vais envoyer contre eux l’épée, la famine et la peste, et je les rendrai pareils à des figues pourries, si mauvaises qu’on ne peut pas les manger.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Je vais envoyer contre eux la guerre, la famine et la maladie. Je les rendrai pareils à des figues pourries qui sont trop mauvaises pour qu’on les mange.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Tazama, ninatuma juu yao upanga, njaa na tauni, nami nitawafanya kama tini mbovu zisizoweza kuliwa kwa sababu ya ubaya [wake].
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Ninakaribia kutuma upanga, njaa na tauni dhidi yao, nami nitawafanya kama tini zilizooza, mbaya kiasi kwamba haziwezi kuliwa.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Nitatuma vita, njaa na magonjwa dhidi yao. Nitawafanya kama tini zilizooza ambazo ni mbaya mno kuliwa.

decisions.choice: thus says the LORD of hosts: the formula repeated
decisions.reason: Verse 16 began "thus says the LORD" and named those the message concerns; the formula is said again here before the message itself.

decisions.choice: like figs that cannot be eaten: the bad figs of chapter 24
decisions.reason: In the vision of the two baskets, the bad figs that could not be eaten stood for Zedekiah, his officials and those left in Jerusalem (24:2, 8). The letter applies that vision here, though it uses a different word for "bad".

decisions.choice: horrid: disgusting, rotten
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It seems to be related to a word for something horrible or shocking (5:30; 23:14), and so means figs so spoiled that they disgust anyone who sees them.

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence (Literal); sword, famine and plague (Balanced); war, famine and disease (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this triad throughout Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: rotten figs
decisions.reason: Literal says "horrid" for the rare word (m3); Balanced and Readable say "rotten", which is what such figs are.

source.text: וְרָֽדַפְתִּי֙ אַֽחֲרֵיהֶ֔ם בַּחֶ֖רֶב בָּרָעָ֣ב וּבַדָּ֑בֶר וּנְתַתִּ֨ים לְזַעֲוָ֜ה לְכֹ֣ל׀מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֗רֶץ לְאָלָ֤ה וּלְשַׁמָּה֙ וְלִשְׁרֵקָ֣ה וּלְחֶרְפָּ֔ה בְּכָל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־הִדַּחְתִּ֥ים שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will pursue after them with the sword, with the famine and with the pestilence, and I will make them for a horror to all [the] kingdoms of the earth, for a curse and for a desolation and for a hissing and for a reproach among all the nations where I have driven them there,

en.L: And I will pursue them with the sword, with famine and with pestilence, and I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, an execration and an appalling thing and a hissing and a reproach among all the nations where I have driven them,
en.B: I will pursue them with sword, famine and plague, and I will make them a horror to every kingdom on earth. Among all the nations where I have driven them, they will be a name used in curses, a thing that appalls, an object of scorn and a disgrace,
en.R: I will chase after them with war, famine and disease. All the kingdoms of the earth will be horrified at what happens to them. In all the nations where I scatter them, people will use their name as a curse. People will be shocked at them, mock them and insult them.

es.L: Y los perseguiré con la espada, con el hambre y con la peste, y los pondré por horror a todos los reinos de la tierra, por maldición, y por espanto, y por burla, y por oprobio entre todas las naciones adonde los he arrojado,
es.B: Los perseguiré con la espada, el hambre y la peste, y haré de ellos un horror para todos los reinos de la tierra. Entre todas las naciones adonde los he arrojado serán un nombre que se usa para maldecir, algo que espanta, un objeto de burla y una vergüenza,
es.R: Los perseguiré con la guerra, el hambre y las enfermedades. Todos los reinos de la tierra se horrorizarán por lo que les pasará. En todas las naciones adonde los disperse, la gente usará su nombre para maldecir. La gente se espantará al verlos, se burlará de ellos y los insultará.

fr.L: Et je les poursuivrai avec l’épée, avec la famine et avec la peste, et je ferai d’eux une horreur pour tous les royaumes de la terre, une exécration, un objet de stupeur, un objet de sifflements et un opprobre parmi toutes les nations où je les ai chassés,
fr.B: Je les poursuivrai par l’épée, la famine et la peste, et je ferai d’eux un objet d’horreur pour tous les royaumes de la terre. Parmi toutes les nations où je les ai chassés, ils seront un nom qu’on utilise pour maudire, un objet de stupeur, de moquerie et de honte,
fr.R: Je les poursuivrai par la guerre, la famine et la maladie. Tous les royaumes de la terre seront horrifiés de ce qui leur arrivera. Dans toutes les nations où je les disperserai, les gens se serviront de leur nom pour maudire. Les gens seront choqués en les voyant, se moqueront d’eux et les insulteront.

sw.L: Nami nitawafuatia kwa upanga, kwa njaa na kwa tauni, nami nitawafanya kuwa kitisho kwa falme zote za dunia, kiapo cha laana, na kitu cha kushangaza, na [kitu cha] kuzomewa, na aibu kati ya mataifa yote nilikowafukuzia,
sw.B: Nitawafuatia kwa upanga, njaa na tauni, nami nitawafanya kuwa kitisho kwa kila ufalme duniani. Kati ya mataifa yote nilikowafukuzia, watakuwa jina linalotumiwa katika laana, kitu cha kushangaza, kitu cha kudharauliwa na aibu,
sw.R: Nitawafukuza kwa vita, njaa na magonjwa. Falme zote za dunia zitaogopa kwa yale yatakayowapata. Katika mataifa yote nitakakowatawanya, watu watalitumia jina lao kama laana. Watu watashtuka wakiwaona, watawadhihaki na kuwatukana.

decisions.choice: horror: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: As in 24:9, the written consonants (ketiv) put two letters of this word in a different order; the scribes marked the usual form to be read aloud (qere). Both name the same word.

decisions.choice: a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, a curse and a reproach: the covenant warnings fulfilled
decisions.reason: Moses warned that Israel would become a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth (Deuteronomy 28:25) and a byword among the nations (Deuteronomy 28:37). Jeremiah repeats the words in 15:4, 24:9 and 34:17.

decisions.choice: an appalling thing: a desolation that stuns those who see it
decisions.reason: The word means both a ruin and the shock it causes, as in 19:8. Those who see what has happened to them will be appalled.

decisions.choice: a hissing: the sound people made at a sight of ruin, in shock and scorn
decisions.reason: Passers-by hissed or whistled at a ruined place or people, a gesture of horror and of mockery (18:16; 19:8; Lamentations 2:15).

decisions.choice: horror; an execration (Balanced: a name used in curses); an appalling thing (Balanced: a thing that appalls); hissing (Balanced: object of scorn); reproach (Balanced: disgrace); Readable in sentences
decisions.reason: The curse word follows the wording set for these lists (42:18; 44:12). "Horror" is kept for the first word, as in 24:9, so the third word, which 19:8 calls a horror, is here "an appalling thing". The hissing follows the book's wording (19:8). Readable says what each word means in sentences of its own.

decisions.choice: two sentences; the nations first in the second
decisions.reason: Balanced divides the verse into two sentences and ends with a comma, since verse 19 gives the reason. Readable uses short sentences and says "scatter" for "drive".

decisions.choice: kiapo cha laana (Literal); jina linalotumiwa katika laana (Balanced); laana (Readable)
decisions.reason: *'Alah* in the curse lists, at each level as the English note sets ("an execration" / "a name used in curses" / "a curse"), worded as in 42:18 and 44:12.

decisions.choice: "une exécration" (L); "un nom qu'on utilise pour maudire" (B); "se serviront de leur nom pour maudire" (R)
decisions.reason: 'Alah in the curse lists as the Jeremiah note sets it; "objet de sifflements / de moquerie" as for shereqah elsewhere.

source.text: תַּ֛חַת אֲשֶֽׁר־לֹא־שָׁמְע֥וּ אֶל־דְּבָרַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֩ שָׁלַ֨חְתִּי אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת־עֲבָדַ֤י הַנְּבִאִים֙ הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם וְשָׁלֹ֔חַ וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: because that not they listened to my words, declaration of Yahweh, which I sent to them [by] my servants the prophets, rising early and sending, and not you listened, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: because they did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which I sent to them by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets, rising early and sending; and you did not listen, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: because they have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the words I sent them through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets, again and again. And you did not listen either, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: This is because they would not listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Over and over I sent {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets to them with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} message. And you exiles did not listen either, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: por cuanto no escucharon {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que les envié por medio de {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} siervos los profetas, madrugando y enviando; y no {{plural_you:escucharon|escuchasteis}}, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: porque no han escuchado {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, las palabras que les envié una y otra vez por medio de {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} siervos los profetas. Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} tampoco {{plural_you:escucharon|escuchasteis}}, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Esto es porque no quisieron escuchar {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Una y otra vez les envié a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} siervos los profetas con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mensaje. Y {{plural_you:ustedes, los desterrados, tampoco escucharon|vosotros, los desterrados, tampoco escuchasteis}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: parce qu’ils n’ont pas écouté {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, que je leur ai envoyées par {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} serviteurs les prophètes, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} levant de bonne heure et [les] envoyant ; et vous n’avez pas écouté, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: parce qu’ils n’ont pas écouté {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, les paroles que je leur ai envoyées sans relâche par {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} serviteurs les prophètes. Et vous non plus, vous n’avez pas écouté, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Cela arrivera parce qu’ils n’ont pas voulu écouter {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Encore et encore, je leur ai envoyé {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} serviteurs les prophètes avec {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} message. Et vous, les exilés, vous n’avez pas écouté non plus, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: kwa sababu hawakuyasikiliza maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, niliyowapelekea kwa watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} manabii, nikiamka mapema na kuwatuma; nanyi hamkusikiliza, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: kwa sababu hawakuyasikiliza maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, maneno niliyowapelekea kupitia watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} manabii tena na tena. Nanyi pia hamkusikiliza, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Hii ni kwa sababu hawakutaka kusikiliza maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Mara nyingi sana niliwatuma watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} manabii kwao na ujumbe {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Nanyi mliohamishwa hamkusikiliza pia, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: rising early and sending: sending again and again, without giving up
decisions.reason: As in 7:13 and 7:25, the phrase pictures someone who starts work early each day and keeps at it.

decisions.choice: my servants the prophets: those who served God by bringing his word
decisions.reason: As in 7:25, the title honors the prophets as God's messengers (25:4; 26:5; 35:15).

decisions.choice: and you did not listen: the exiles too
decisions.reason: The verse speaks first of those in Jerusalem ("they") and then turns to the exiles hearing the letter ("you"). The exiles had not listened either, which is why they too had been sent away; now they must not repeat that by trusting their prophets (verses 8-9, 20).

decisions.choice: rising early and sending (Literal); again and again (Balanced); over and over (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase throughout Jeremiah. "Servants" is kept at every level for the prophets, as in 7:25.

decisions.choice: you exiles; with my message
decisions.reason: Readable says who "you" are (m3) and what the prophets brought.

source.text: וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר־יְהוָ֑ה כָּל־הַ֨גּוֹלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־שִׁלַּ֥חְתִּי מִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you, hear [the] word of Yahweh, all the exile whom I sent from Jerusalem to Babylon.

en.L: And you, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all the exiles whom I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon.
en.B: But you, all you exiles whom I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: So now, all of you captives whom I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon, listen to the message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:oigan|oíd}} la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, todos los del destierro que envié de Jerusalén a Babilonia.
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, todos los desterrados que envié de Jerusalén a Babilonia, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}} la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Así que ahora, todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los prisioneros que envié de Jerusalén a Babilonia, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}} este mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et vous, écoutez la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, vous tous, exilés que j’ai envoyés de Jérusalem à Babylone.
fr.B: Mais vous, tous les exilés que j’ai envoyés de Jérusalem à Babylone, écoutez la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Alors maintenant, vous tous, les prisonniers que j’ai envoyés de Jérusalem à Babylone, écoutez le message {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Nanyi, sikieni neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ninyi mateka wote niliowatuma kutoka Yerusalemu mpaka Babeli.
sw.B: Lakini ninyi, ninyi mateka wote niliowatoa Yerusalemu kuwapeleka Babeli, sikilizeni neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Basi sasa, ninyi nyote mliochukuliwa mateka, niliowatoa Yerusalemu kuwapeleka Babeli, sikilizeni ujumbe huu kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: and you: an emphatic turn to the exiles
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out: "as for you". Unlike those who would not listen (verse 19), the exiles are called to hear now; the word they are to hear follows in verses 21-23.

decisions.choice: whom I sent away: a gentler word than "exiled"
decisions.reason: The verb means to send off or let go. It is used of the exiles in 24:5, and it again makes God the one who sent them.

decisions.choice: the address first, then the command
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the long address before "hear", as English does. Readable says "So now" to mark the turn.

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶל־אַחְאָ֤ב בֶּן־קֽוֹלָיָה֙ וְאֶל־צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בֶן־מַֽעֲשֵׂיָ֔ה הַֽנִּבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶ֛ם בִּשְׁמִ֖י שָׁ֑קֶר הִנְנִ֣י׀נֹתֵ֣ן אֹתָ֗ם בְּיַד֙ נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל וְהִכָּ֖ם לְעֵינֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel, concerning Ahab son of Kolaiah and concerning Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, the [ones] prophesying to you in my name falsehood: Behold, I [am] giving them into [the] hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he will strike them before your eyes.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning Ahab son of Kolaiah and concerning Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying a lie to you in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name: Look, I am giving them into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he will strike them down before your eyes.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this about Ahab son of Kolaiah and about Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying lies to you in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name: I am about to hand them over to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he will put them to death before your eyes.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says about Ahab son of Kolaiah and about Zedekiah son of Maaseiah. They are using {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name to tell you lies. I am going to hand them over to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he will kill them while you watch.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, el Dios de Israel, acerca de Acab hijo de Colaías y acerca de Sedequías hijo de Maasías, que {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizan mentira en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre: He aquí, yo los entrego en mano de Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, y él los herirá delante de {{plural_you:sus ojos|vuestros ojos}}.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel, dice esto acerca de Acab hijo de Colaías y acerca de Sedequías hijo de Maasías, que {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizan mentiras en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre: Voy a entregarlos en manos de Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, y él los matará delante de {{plural_you:sus ojos|vuestros ojos}}.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel, acerca de Acab hijo de Colaías y acerca de Sedequías hijo de Maasías. Ellos están usando {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre para {{plural_you:decirles|deciros}} mentiras. Voy a entregarlos a Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, y él los matará mientras {{plural_you:ustedes miran|vosotros miráis}}.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, au sujet d’Achab fils de Qolaya et au sujet de Sédécias fils de Maaséya, qui vous prophétisent le mensonge en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom : Voici, je les livre entre les mains de Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, et il les frappera sous vos yeux.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, dit ceci au sujet d’Achab fils de Qolaya et de Sédécias fils de Maaséya, qui vous prophétisent des mensonges en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom : Je vais les livrer à Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, et il les mettra à mort sous vos yeux.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, au sujet d’Achab, fils de Qolaya, et de Sédécias, fils de Maaséya. Ils se servent de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom pour vous dire des mensonges. Je vais les livrer à Nabuchodonosor, le roi de Babylone, et il les tuera sous vos yeux.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, asema hivi kuhusu Ahabu mwana wa Kolaya, na kuhusu Sedekia mwana wa Maaseya, wanaowatabiria uongo kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}: Tazama, nitawatia mkononi mwa Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli, naye atawapiga mbele ya macho yenu.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, asemavyo kuhusu Ahabu mwana wa Kolaya na Sedekia mwana wa Maaseya, wanaowatabiria uongo kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}: Ninakaribia kuwatia mikononi mwa Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli, naye atawaua mbele ya macho yenu.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, analosema kuhusu Ahabu mwana wa Kolaya na Sedekia mwana wa Maaseya. Wanalitumia jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} kuwaambia uongo. Nitawatia mikononi mwa Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli, naye atawaua mkiwa mnatazama.

decisions.choice: Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah: two prophets among the exiles
decisions.reason: These two men are known only from this passage. This Zedekiah is not the king of verse 3; the name was common. They were among the prophets in Babylon of verse 15.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar: the form of the name with r
decisions.reason: Verses 1 and 3 spell the king's name Nebuchadnezzar; this verse has the form Nebuchadrezzar used in most of Jeremiah (see 25:1). It is the same king.

decisions.choice: giving them into the hand of: handing them over to the power of
decisions.reason: To give someone into another's hand is to put that person in the other's power, here for punishment (21:7; 22:25).

decisions.choice: he will strike them: he will put them to death
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike, and often to kill. Verse 22 says how they died. The text does not say why the king of Babylon would execute them; prophets who promised a quick end to Babylon's rule (verses 8-9; 28:2-4) could well be seen as stirring up revolt. Verse 23 gives God's reason.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar
decisions.reason: Each verse keeps the form of the name its Hebrew uses (m2).

decisions.choice: hand them over; put them to death (Balanced); kill them while you watch (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idioms mean in plain English (m3, m4).

decisions.choice: Nabucodorosor
decisions.reason: Within this letter the Hebrew switches from the -n- form (verses 1 and 3) to the -r- form here; each verse keeps the form its Hebrew has, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Nebukadreza
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew spells the name with r again, so Swahili follows it, as in 21-25; the false prophet Sedekia mwana wa Maaseya is not the king.

decisions.choice: "Achab fils de Qolaya", "Sédécias fils de Maaséya"
decisions.reason: These two prophets bear the same names as the king of Israel and the king of Judah, so French uses the same forms, "Achab" and "Sédécias", as the Hebrew does.

source.text: וְלֻקַּ֤ח מֵהֶם֙ קְלָלָ֔ה לְכֹל֙ גָּל֣וּת יְהוּדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּבָבֶ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר יְשִֽׂמְךָ֤ יְהוָה֙ כְּצִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ וּכְאֶחָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר־קָלָ֥ם מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will be taken from them a curse by all [the] exile of Judah who [are] in Babylon, saying: May make you Yahweh like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom roasted them [the] king of Babylon in the fire,

en.L: And from them a curse will be taken up by all the exiles of Judah who [are] in Babylon, saying, 'May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire,'
en.B: Their fate will become a curse that all the exiles of Judah in Babylon will use: 'May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, the men the king of Babylon roasted alive in the fire,'
en.R: All the captives from Judah who are in Babylon will use their names when they curse someone. They will say, 'May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make you end up like Zedekiah and Ahab, who were burned to death by the king of Babylon!'

es.L: Y de ellos se tomará una maldición entre todos los desterrados de Judá que [están] en Babilonia, diciendo: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te haga como a Sedequías y como a Acab, a quienes el rey de Babilonia asó en el fuego”,
es.B: Su destino se convertirá en una maldición que usarán todos los desterrados de Judá que están en Babilonia: “Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te haga como a Sedequías y a Acab, los hombres que el rey de Babilonia asó vivos en el fuego”,
es.R: Todos los prisioneros de Judá que están en Babilonia usarán sus nombres cuando maldigan a alguien. Dirán: “¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te haga terminar como Sedequías y Acab, a quienes el rey de Babilonia quemó vivos!”.

fr.L: Et d’eux on tirera une malédiction parmi tous les exilés de Juda qui [sont] à Babylone, en disant : “Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} te traite comme Sédécias et comme Achab, que le roi de Babylone a grillés au feu”,
fr.B: Leur sort deviendra une formule de malédiction pour tous les exilés de Juda qui sont à Babylone : “Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} te traite comme Sédécias et Achab, que le roi de Babylone a fait rôtir vifs dans le feu”,
fr.R: Tous les prisonniers de Juda qui sont à Babylone se serviront de leurs noms quand ils voudront maudire quelqu’un. Ils diront : “Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} te fasse finir comme Sédécias et Achab, que le roi de Babylone a fait brûler vifs !”

sw.L: Na kwao laana itachukuliwa na mateka wote wa Yuda walioko Babeli, wakisema, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na akufanye kama Sedekia na kama Ahabu, ambao mfalme wa Babeli aliwaoka motoni,'
sw.B: Mwisho wao utakuwa laana ambayo mateka wote wa Yuda walioko Babeli wataitumia: '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na akufanye kama Sedekia na Ahabu, watu ambao mfalme wa Babeli aliwachoma motoni wakiwa hai,'
sw.R: Mateka wote kutoka Yuda walioko Babeli watalitumia jina lao wanapomlaani mtu. Watasema, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na akufanye uishie kama Sedekia na Ahabu, waliochomwa moto mpaka kufa na mfalme wa Babeli!'

decisions.choice: a curse ... roasted: a play on words
decisions.reason: The word for "curse" (qelalah) sounds like the verb "roasted" (qalah), and both echo the name of Ahab's father, Kolaiah. The men's very fate becomes the curse people speak.

decisions.choice: roasted in the fire: burned to death, a Babylonian punishment
decisions.reason: Babylonian law named burning as the penalty for some crimes, and Daniel 3 tells of a furnace used to put men to death (Daniel 3:6, 19-23). The two prophets were burned alive.

decisions.choice: a curse will be taken from them: their fate will be used as a curse
decisions.reason: People will take the two men as the pattern for a curse: "may you end up like them". It is what 24:9 and verse 18 mean by a people becoming "a curse" (compare Isaiah 65:15).

decisions.choice: single quotation marks; the sentence runs on into verse 23
decisions.reason: The curse is quoted inside the letter, so it takes single marks. Literal and Balanced end with a comma, since verse 23 gives the reason; Readable ends the sentence here.

decisions.choice: roasted alive (Balanced); burned to death (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "alive" and Readable says plainly what "roasted in the fire" meant (m2); both leave out the second "like", which English does not need.

source.text: יַ֡עַן אֲשֶׁר֩ עָשׂ֨וּ נְבָלָ֜ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיְנַֽאֲפוּ֙ אֶת־נְשֵׁ֣י רֵֽעֵיהֶ֔ם וַיְדַבְּר֨וּ דָבָ֤ר בִּשְׁמִי֙ שֶׁ֔קֶר אֲשֶׁ֖ר ל֣וֹא צִוִּיתִ֑ם וְאָנֹכִ֛י הַיּוֹדֵ֥עַוָעֵ֖ד נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: because that they did folly in Israel, and they committed adultery with [the] wives of their neighbors, and they spoke a word in my name [of] falsehood, which not I commanded them; and I [am] the [one] knowing and witness, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: because they have done an outrage in Israel, and they have committed adultery with their neighbors' wives, and they have spoken in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name a lying word, which I did not command them; and I [am] the one who knows, and [I am] witness, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: because they have done a disgraceful thing in Israel. They have committed adultery with their neighbors' wives and have spoken lies in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, words I did not command them to speak. I am the one who knows it, and I am witness to it, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: This will happen because they have done shameful things in Israel. They have slept with other men's wives. And they have told lies and said that the messages came from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, when I never told them to say anything. I know all about it, and I am a witness to it, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

es.L: porque cometieron una infamia en Israel, y cometieron adulterio con las mujeres de sus prójimos, y hablaron en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre palabra mentirosa, que no les mandé; y yo [soy] el que sabe, y [soy] testigo, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».
es.B: porque hicieron algo vergonzoso en Israel. Cometieron adulterio con las mujeres de sus vecinos y dijeron mentiras en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, palabras que yo no les mandé decir. Yo soy el que lo sabe, y soy testigo de ello, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».
es.R: Esto pasará porque han hecho cosas vergonzosas en Israel. Se han acostado con las esposas de otros hombres. Y han dicho mentiras, afirmando que los mensajes venían de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, cuando yo nunca les mandé decir nada. Yo lo sé todo, y soy testigo de ello, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».

fr.L: parce qu’ils ont commis une infamie en Israël, qu’ils ont commis l’adultère avec les femmes de leurs prochains, et qu’ils ont dit en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom une parole de mensonge, ce que je ne leur avais pas ordonné ; et c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui sais, et [je suis] témoin, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. »
fr.B: parce qu’ils ont commis une infamie en Israël. Ils ont commis l’adultère avec les femmes de leurs prochains et ont dit des mensonges en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, des paroles que je ne leur avais pas ordonné de dire. C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui le sais, et j’en suis témoin, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. »
fr.R: Cela arrivera parce qu’ils ont fait des choses honteuses en Israël. Ils ont couché avec les femmes d’autres hommes. Ils ont dit des mensonges en prétendant que ces messages venaient de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, alors que je ne leur avais jamais rien dit de dire. Je sais tout cela, et j’en suis témoin, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. »

sw.L: kwa sababu wamefanya upumbavu katika Israeli, nao wamezini na wake za jirani zao, nao wamenena kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} neno la uongo, nisilowaamuru; nami [ndimi] ninayejua, nami [ni] shahidi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.B: kwa sababu wametenda jambo la aibu katika Israeli. Wamezini na wake za jirani zao na kusema uongo kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, maneno ambayo sikuwaamuru kusema. Mimi ndiye ninayejua, nami ni shahidi wa jambo hilo, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.R: Hilo litatokea kwa sababu wametenda mambo ya aibu katika Israeli. Wamelala na wake za watu wengine. Tena wamesema uongo na kudai kwamba ujumbe wao ulitoka {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, wakati sikuwaambia waseme lolote. Ninajua yote kuhusu jambo hilo, nami ni shahidi wake, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."

decisions.choice: the one who knows: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) can be read "he knows"; the scribes marked "the one who knows" to be read aloud (qere). Both say that God himself knows what they have done.

decisions.choice: an outrage: a shameful act that breaks the bonds of the community
decisions.reason: The word names a deed so gross that it disgraces the whole people, often a sexual crime (Genesis 34:7; Deuteronomy 22:21; Judges 20:6, 10) or a breach of what is holy (Joshua 7:15). "In Israel" means among God's people.

decisions.choice: adultery with their neighbors' wives: a breach of the commandments
decisions.reason: The law forbade adultery and desire for a neighbor's wife (Exodus 20:14, 17). Jeremiah had charged the prophets of Jerusalem with the same sin (23:14).

decisions.choice: I am the one who knows and the witness
decisions.reason: In a court a witness testifies to what he has seen. God himself has seen what these men did, even if it was hidden from others, and he will testify against them (compare Malachi 3:5; Micah 1:2).

decisions.choice: a closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: The letter that began in verse 4 ends here.

decisions.choice: slept with other men's wives; told lies and said that the messages came from me
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what adultery is and what speaking lies in God's name means. "I never told them to say anything" gives "which I did not command them".

source.text: וְאֶל־שְׁמַעְיָ֥הוּ הַנֶּחֱלָמִ֖י תֹּאמַ֥ר לֵאמֹֽר׃

decisions.choice: and to Shemaiah you shall say: God now speaks to Jeremiah
decisions.reason: A new section starts without an introduction. The "you" is singular: God tells Jeremiah what to say to Shemaiah, a prophet among the exiles who had written to Jerusalem in reply to Jeremiah's letter. The speech is broken off at verse 28 and finished in verses 31-32.

decisions.choice: the Nehelamite: of an unknown place or family
decisions.reason: The word names where Shemaiah or his family came from, but no place called Nehelam is known. It sounds like the word for "dream", and some think it may be a nickname for a man who trusted dreams (verse 8), but this cannot be shown.

decisions.choice: an opening quotation mark
decisions.reason: God's words to Jeremiah are quoted from here to verse 28. The message to Shemaiah inside them takes single marks, his letter double marks again, and the words he quotes from Jeremiah single marks.

decisions.choice: Give this message to
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "you shall say, saying" means.

decisions.choice: Semaías el nehelamita
decisions.reason: The name and its unknown place-name keep the forms the terms note sets.

decisions.choice: because you sent: a sentence left unfinished
decisions.reason: The sentence begins "because" but never reaches its "therefore". The quotation of Shemaiah's letter runs on to verse 28, and the judgment comes only in verses 31-32, where "because ... therefore" is spoken in full.

decisions.choice: in your own name: on your own authority
decisions.reason: The other prophets spoke falsely "in my name" (verses 9, 21, 23). Shemaiah wrote in his own name, giving orders to the priests in Jerusalem without any word from God.

decisions.choice: Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest: the second-ranking priest in the temple
decisions.reason: Zephaniah was the "second priest", next to the chief priest (52:24), and King Zedekiah twice sent him to ask Jeremiah for a word from the LORD (21:1; 37:3). He was put to death by the Babylonians after Jerusalem fell (52:24-27).

decisions.choice: You sent letters ... You wrote:
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the charge without "because", since the sentence it begins is not finished (m1), and say "You wrote" for "saying". Readable breaks the verse into short sentences.

fr.R: ‘{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a fait prêtre à la place du prêtre Yehoyada. C’est toi le responsable dans le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. sw.L: "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekufanya kuhani mahali pa Yehoyada kuhani, ili kuwe na wasimamizi katika nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} juu ya kila mtu mwenye wazimu ajifanyaye nabii, nawe umtie katika mkatale na katika kongwa.

decisions.choice: Jehoiada the priest: probably the priest who guarded the temple for young King Joash
decisions.reason: Jehoiada led the overthrow of Queen Athaliah and set guards over the house of the LORD (2 Kings 11:4-18). Shemaiah may name him as the model of a priest who kept order in the temple, or he may mean a later priest of that name, perhaps Zephaniah's predecessor, of whom nothing else is known.

decisions.choice: to be overseers: the priest and the officers under him
decisions.reason: The noun is plural. Zephaniah and the priests with him are to be the temple's officers. Pashhur had held this office of overseer when he put Jeremiah in the stocks (20:1-2).

decisions.choice: mad and acting the prophet: a sneer at prophets
decisions.reason: The first word means insane, raving. It was used in scorn of prophets (2 Kings 9:11; Hosea 9:7). The verb form for "prophesy" can describe raving behavior (1 Samuel 18:10). Shemaiah means any wild man who claims to speak for God.

decisions.choice: the stocks and the collar: devices for holding a prisoner
decisions.reason: The stocks are the device in which Pashhur held Jeremiah (20:2). The second word is found only here. It may name a collar or iron band for the neck; some take it as a narrow cell.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for Shemaiah's letter
decisions.reason: Shemaiah's letter is quoted inside the LORD's message to him, which is quoted inside the LORD's words to Jeremiah, so it takes double marks again.

decisions.choice: sets himself up as a prophet, neck irons (Balanced); acts like a prophet, iron collar (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the scorn in the verb (m3) and say what the collar was. Readable says "crazy person" for the madman and begins new sentences.

decisions.choice: ‘ ’ for Shemaiah's letter
decisions.reason: Shemaiah's letter is the third level of speech (the LORD to Jeremiah « », the message to Shemaiah “ ”), so it takes ‘ ’; its quotation of Jeremiah in verse 28 is put in “ ” again.

decisions.choice: "aux ceps et au carcan" (L, B); "dans les ceps, avec un collier de fer autour du cou" (R)
decisions.reason: "Ceps" as in 20:2; the second device held the neck, which "carcan" names.

decisions.choice: rebuked: reprimanded and restrained
decisions.reason: The verb means to rebuke sharply, and so to check or restrain. Shemaiah wants Zephaniah to use his authority against Jeremiah, as verse 26 says.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah of Anathoth: the prophet named by his home village
decisions.reason: Anathoth was a town of priests a few miles north of Jerusalem, Jeremiah's home (1:1; 11:21-23). Naming him by his village, not as a prophet, may be meant to belittle him.

decisions.choice: who acts the prophet: the same verb form as in verse 26
decisions.reason: Shemaiah uses the word he used for the madman, so he counts Jeremiah among them.

decisions.choice: sets himself up as a prophet (Balanced); acting like a prophet (Readable); among you
decisions.reason: As in verse 26. Balanced and Readable say "among you", since Jeremiah prophesied in Jerusalem, where Zephaniah was.

decisions.choice: for therefore: "for he has even" or "for this reason"
alternatives: for that is why he sent to us
decisions.reason: The words are literally "for therefore". They may stress how far Jeremiah has gone ("he has even sent to us"), or say that because no one stopped him he has been able to send his letter. The point is the same: Shemaiah treats the letter as proof that Jeremiah must be silenced.

decisions.choice: it will be long; build houses ...: Shemaiah quotes Jeremiah's letter
decisions.reason: Shemaiah quotes verse 5 and sums up verse 10 as "it will be long". The word for long is feminine, and its subject is not named; the exile, or the time of waiting, is meant.

decisions.choice: the end of Shemaiah's letter and of the LORD's broken-off speech
decisions.reason: The quotation of Shemaiah's letter ends here. The message the LORD began in verse 25 is not finished; verse 29 goes back to the story, and verses 31-32 give the judgment.

decisions.choice: indirect speech
decisions.reason: Readable reports Jeremiah's words in Shemaiah's letter without a further set of quotation marks, which would be hard to follow. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: closing quotation marks
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced close Jeremiah's words, Shemaiah's letter, the LORD's message and the LORD's words to Jeremiah, in that order; Readable has one set fewer (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: edifiquen, habiten, planten, coman (no plural_you span)
decisions.reason: Here Shemaiah quotes Jeremiah's letter to the exiles inside his own complaint; the plural forms are a quotation of a quotation and are left without a reader setting, since the "you" is not the reader's.

decisions.choice: because ...: the charge, now spoken in full
decisions.reason: This takes up the unfinished "because" of verse 25 and goes on to the "therefore" of verse 32.

decisions.choice: I did not send him, and he has made you trust in a lie
decisions.reason: The same words were spoken to Hananiah, who broke the yoke from Jeremiah's neck: "the LORD has not sent you, and you have made this people trust in a lie" (28:15). Shemaiah, like Hananiah, is a prophet God did not send.

decisions.choice: has prophesied to you: in his letter
decisions.reason: Shemaiah's letter claimed to speak for God ("the LORD has made you priest", verse 26). This counts as prophesying, though God had not sent him.

decisions.choice: God's words to Jeremiah in double marks, the message to the exiles in single marks
decisions.reason: The message Jeremiah is to send is quoted inside God's words to him, as in 7:2. Readable ends the sentence here and starts verse 32 with "So".

records.literal_gloss: therefore thus says Yahweh: Behold, I [am] visiting upon Shemaiah the Nehelamite and upon his offspring; not will be to him a man dwelling in [the] midst of the people the this, and not he will see the good that I [am] doing for my people, declaration of Yahweh, for rebellion he has spoken against Yahweh.

en.L: therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am visiting [punishment] on Shemaiah the Nehelamite and on his offspring. He will not have anyone living among this people, and he will not see the good that I am doing for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for he has spoken rebellion against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"
en.B: therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am about to punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. No one of his line will be left living among this people, and he will not see the good that I am going to do for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because he has preached rebellion against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. None of his family will be left among this people. He will not live to see the good things I am going to do for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This is because he has told people to turn against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"

es.L: por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: He aquí, yo castigaré a Semaías el nehelamita y a su descendencia. es.B: por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Voy a castigar a Semaías el nehelamita y a sus descendientes. es.R: Por eso, esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Castigaré a Semaías el nehelamita y a sus descendientes. No quedará nadie de su familia entre este pueblo. Él no vivirá para ver las cosas buenas que voy a hacer por {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Esto es porque le ha dicho a la gente que se rebele contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}”».

fr.L: c’est pourquoi ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Voici, je vais punir Shemaya le Néhélamite et sa descendance. Il n’aura personne qui habite au milieu de ce peuple, et il ne verra pas le bien que je vais faire à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, car il a prêché la révolte contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.” »
fr.B: c’est pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Je vais punir Shemaya le Néhélamite et sa descendance. Il ne vivra pas assez longtemps pour voir le bien que je vais faire à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Car il a poussé les gens à se révolter contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.” »

decisions.choice: I am visiting on: I will punish
decisions.reason: The verb that in verse 10 meant God's coming to help means here, with "on", his coming to punish.

decisions.choice: he will not have anyone dwelling among this people: his family line will be cut off
decisions.reason: No descendant of his will be among God's people when they are restored. He promised a quick return and will have no share in the real one.

decisions.choice: the good that I am doing for my people: the restoration promised in verses 10-14
decisions.reason: The "good" is the "good word" of verse 10: the return from exile. The participle describes God's plan as already under way.

decisions.choice: he has spoken rebellion against the LORD: the charge against a false prophet
decisions.reason: The law says that a prophet who speaks rebellion against the LORD is to die (Deuteronomy 13:6), and Jeremiah used these words of Hananiah (28:16).

decisions.choice: punish (Balanced, Readable); preached rebellion (Balanced); told people to turn against (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "visiting" and brackets the punishment it implies; Balanced and Readable say "punish". "Spoken rebellion" means urging people to turn from the LORD.

decisions.choice: closing quotation marks
decisions.reason: The message to the exiles and the LORD's words to Jeremiah both end here.
